messages:
maya: quick sanity check — wiring KMS decrypt to an IRSA-backed role for logging-sa (namespace=logging). pod fails with AccessDenied: "User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt" when trying to decrypt a data key. TF snippet below, any obvious red flags?

maya: ```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "logging_irsa_role" {
  name = "redwood-logging-irsa"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_assume_policy.json
}

resource "aws_iam_policy" "kms_decrypt_policy" {
  name = "redwood-kms-decrypt"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17"
    Statement = [{
      Effect = "Allow"
      Action = ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"]
      Resource = aws_kms_key.logging_key.arn
    }]
  })
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "attach_kms" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.logging_irsa_role.name
  policy_arn = aws_iam_policy.kms_decrypt_policy.arn
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "logging_key" {
  description = "logging data key"
  policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.kms_policy.json
}
```

rohit: couple quick asks — are you using an aws_kms_grant resource or relying solely on the key policy + IAM policy?

maya: relying on key policy + IAM policy for now. key policy (data.aws_iam_policy_document.kms_policy) currently allows admin principals and has a statement allowing the account root and a few roles. didn't add explicit grant.

leo: two things to check: 1) KMS key policy must explicitly allow the IAM principal (role) to use the key unless the account-level policy delegates that. 2) If your code sets an EncryptionContext on encryption, Decrypt requires matching context — but most SDK uses none.

leo: example minimal key policy statement to allow the role:```json
{
  "Sid": "Allow use by logging IRSA role",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-logging-irsa" },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

sam: also for IRSA the principal in the key policy should be the role ARN (not the web identity). the role itself is assumed by the OIDC provider. many teams prefer adding an aws_kms_grant: grants avoid touching key policy and are easier to provision per-role.

sam: grant snippet that worked for us:```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "logging_irsa_grant" {
  name            = "grant-logging-irsa"
  key_id          = aws_kms_key.logging_key.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.logging_irsa_role.arn
  operations      = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  retire_on_delete = true
}
```

maya: ah — I used iam policy only. i'll try adding the grant. thanks. quick Q: terraform plan for the grant shows replacing the key because of rotation window difference? any tips to avoid destructive change?

rohit: we had similar: aws_kms_grant itself shouldn't force key replacement. but if you changed the key resource arguments (e.g., key rotation, policy), plan may want replace. create grant in separate small PR so it applies independently — safer.

maya: makes sense. i'll split into two PRs: 1) create grant, 2) update role policy if still needed. will also add a test pod to exercise decrypt. suggested test command?

sam: you can run a simple job that uses aws-cli:```bash
kubectl run --rm -it kms-test --image=amazonlinux --namespace=logging -- bash -c "yum install -y awscli; aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext --region us-west-2"
```
But easier: create a short Go/python pod that calls GenerateDataKey then Decrypt. make sure serviceAccountName on the pod is the IRSA SA and the SA has iam.amazonaws.com/role: <role-arn> annotation.

leo: and confirm the role is actually attached to the SA in the cluster: `kubectl -n logging get sa logging-sa -o yaml` — check the annotation. sometimes folks create SA but forget to patch the annotation in the deployment manifest.

maya: will do. one more: CI shows terraform plan in PR #482 with a warning about principal formatting (arn vs role name). ci-bot, can you paste the plan snippet?

ci-bot: [automated message] terraform plan for PR #482 — changed resources: + aws_kms_grant.logging_irsa_grant (tainted=false) — no destroys. Warning: principal ARN used in grant resolves to a role that doesn't exist yet in state.

rohit: that warning is expected if role is in the same PR and not applied yet. order of operations: apply role first, then grant. split PRs or add depends_on to be safe.

maya: thanks all — i'll split into two PRs, add aws_kms_grant in the first, plan/apply, then attach policy in follow-up. leaving this thread open in case anything else pops up. :thumbsup:
